critique:
field placed, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Keep the field as it is, with two points made literal so the written value and the policy's value coincide character for character. (1) The value is always written as a JSON array of double-quoted color strings, e.g. [] or ["green", "blue"]; at the first decision step of every episode the value is the literal [] (an explicit empty array, never a blank). (2) The append event is: the execution steps of this decision step contain at least one frame with a cube reported 'is held in the gripper', and the last frame of the step (the scene at the decision step) reports no held cube with the fingers about 100% open. That event is always one completed bin placement, regardless of where the gripper was reported when the fingers opened (it is often 30-50 px from the bin's reported center) and regardless of any same-color cube detection appearing on the table at or near the release point in the same frames; append the held cube's color once. One example sequence over an episode: [] -> [] -> ["green"] -> ["green"] -> ["green", "green"].

field placed, POLICY PROMPT
  Three failures of PREDICTABILITY. First, at the first decision step (no execution steps, empty carried-in memory) the policy left the field blank where the annotation holds []; the instruction must say: when the carried-in memory is empty, write the literal [] as this step's value. Second, in most steps the policy produced the right colors but wrote them Python-style with single quotes; the instruction must say the value is a JSON array of double-quoted strings exactly like the carried-in value and the example, e.g. ["green", "green"], never ['green', 'green']. Third, twice the policy declined to append because the release looked like a miss: the fingers opened with the gripper reported some 40-50 px from the bin's center, and in the same frames a cube of the held color was newly detected on the table near the release point. The instruction must say: the oracle always runs the put-into-bin subgoal to completion, so the pattern 'some execution frame of this step reports a cube held in the gripper, and the last frame reports no held cube with the fingers about 100% open' is always a successful placement; append the held cube's color once, whatever the gripper position at release and whatever cubes appear or move on the table. Value after such a step, e.g. carried-in ["red"] becomes ["red", "red"].

the policy prompt for subgoal
  Four things, in order of how often they broke SUFFICIENCY. (a) Reading the scene. Twice the policy, carrying an empty list and seeing many table cubes, chose a pick even though the last frame of the step reported a cube 'is held in the gripper' with the fingers 46% open and the gripper raised; it had read the earlier open-gripper frames. Rule 1 must say explicitly: the scene at this decision step is the LAST listed observed step; check that frame first, and if any object line there ends in 'is held in the gripper', or the fingers there are partly closed (about 46%), the answer is B before any other rule is considered. (b) Color priority. Rule 3's 'larger remaining count' is wrong and sent the policy to the other color three times. Every recorded episode with two goal colors finishes one color before starting the other: with placed=["green"] under a goal of three blue and two green, the next pick is green again; with placed=["green","green"] under a goal of two red and three green, the next pick is green again. Replace the rule with: if the last entry of `placed` is a color whose required count is not yet met, pick that color; otherwise pick any color that still has fewer entries than required. When `placed` is empty the recorded first choice does not follow the named order nor the larger or smaller count, so the rule should say any needed color is acceptable there. (c) Ghost and drifting detections. Twice the policy pointed at a detection that was not a real resting cube: once a cube of the needed color that first appeared exactly where the just-released cube had been held and whose coordinates shifted frame to frame, once a cube next to the gripper whose coordinates moved along with the gripper. The rule should say: a candidate must be reported as a table cube (not held) at the same coordinates, within about 2 px, in every execution frame of this decision step including the first one; a detection that first appears during the step, that sits where the held cube was last reported, or whose position moves between frames is not a candidate while any stable one exists. (d) Tie-break among several stable cubes of the needed color. The instruction gives none, and the policy picked the first listed or an arbitrary one in seven steps. The recorded choices in this minibatch most often fall on the stable needed-color cube nearest the bin's reported center (in roughly three quarters of the cases), and never on a cube reported within about 25 px of the bin center, so the rule should say: among stable candidates, prefer the one nearest the bin but not overlapping it, and state that the point is the candidate's center as reported in the last frame, which may differ from any single listed coordinate by a pixel or two. The fallback clause 'nearest the gripper' should go, since the recorded picks are not nearest the gripper.

refused
  Several steps asked for one exact geometric rule that reproduces every recorded choice among same-color cubes (nearest the bin, largest y, image center, nearest the gripper). Read across the whole minibatch no single such rule holds: the nearest-bin preference fails in a few steps and every other candidate rule fails more often, so I pass nearest-bin on as a preference, not a guarantee, and do not pass on largest-y, image-center or gripper-nearest. One step asked whether a cube within about 30 px of the bin counts as on the bin; the one such case was also a ghost detection at the release point, so it is covered by the stability rule rather than a distance threshold. One step asked which color to start with when nothing has been placed yet; the three first picks in the minibatch go to the second-named color twice and the first-named once, to the color needing more once and fewer twice, so no rule is supported and I report only that any needed color is allowed there. One step suggested the recorded first-step point was a composite of several detections; it is within 2 px of a listed green cube, so that suggestion stays out.
